The native-to-commit bridge carries all 192 frozen authorized clean proposals unchanged through distinct loopback authorization, gateway, and effect processes. Authorization issues the receipt and propagates revocation, the gateway only relays commit requests, and the effect service verifies and writes SQLite. Each revoked clone observes the version change active, waits 10~ms within a 1,000~ms hold, and then commits. All 384 revoked rows pass this happens-before gate, and all 768 rows preserve the proposal hash through the service boundary. Both policies commit 192/192 stable controls. Cached authorization commits 192/192 stale revoked effects, whereas receipt-bound commits 0/192. Each alias separately yields 48/48 versus 0/48 ($p=7.11\times10^{-15}$; Fig.~\ref{fig:auth_matrix}c). Every allow has one ledger row and every block has none. These are paired clones, not new model samples or a revocation-prevalence estimate.
